conventions.convention: Fréchet spaces are complex, Hausdorff, locally convex spaces with a separating countable seminorm family and complete seminorm uniformity; the zero space is included.
A compact linear map sends some neighborhood of zero to a set with compact closure. A quasi-epimorphism has closed, finite-codimensional image.

Presentation quotient topologies require surjectivity on sections. Čech cochains use increasing index tuples, alternating restriction differentials, finite-product topologies, and cocycle-subspace/coboundary-quotient topologies.
The projective finiteness claim assumes full AC, concerns ordinary right-derived global sections, and is stated for 0 ≤ r ≤ 3 and every q ≥ 0.
The intersection lemma assumes a partial free resolution of length 2r near the closure of a participating polydisc; exactness at the leftmost free term is not required.
On the projective-line overlap, w = 1/z and the O(−2) frames satisfy e₁ = z⁻²e₀; the ordered coboundary is z⁻²b(1/z) − a(z).

load_bearing.statement: Assume full AC. For 0 ≤ r ≤ 3 and every coherent analytic module F on P^r(C), H^q(P^r(C),F) is finite-dimensional over C for every q ≥ 0; its specified Čech quotient topology is Hausdorff and independent of admissible finite cover and local presentations.

Under full AC, a continuous cochain map of Fréchet complexes that is compact in degree q and surjective on degree-q cohomology has Hausdorff finite-dimensional target cohomology. Any surjective cohomology map induced by a continuous cochain map of Fréchet complexes is open.

Under full AC, a finite presentation on a chart-open set with surjective section map induces a Fréchet quotient topology; the stated presentation, chart, and countable compatible-family constructions are independent of choices.

Under full AC and the stated local Oka interface, a nonempty finite intersection of relatively compact coordinate polydiscs is acyclic for F when a neighborhood of the closure of one participating polydisc carries the stated length-2r partial free resolution of F; disconnected intersections are handled componentwise.

Under full AC, restriction from Ω to Ω′ with compact closure in Ω is compact for the specified coherent-section quotient topologies, assuming a finite presentation on Ω and surjective presentation section maps on both opens.
Under full AC, if g:E→F is a continuous linear quasi-epimorphism between complex Fréchet spaces and h:E→F is compact and continuous linear, then g+h is a quasi-epimorphism.
Every holomorphic f on C* has a unique decomposition f(z)=g(z)+az⁻¹+z⁻²h(1/z), with g,h entire and a∈C.

seams_checked.note: The consuming Oka interfaces preserve full AC, coherent-kernel closure, and finite local partial resolutions without asserting leftmost exactness or global free resolutions.

Local polydisc vanishing is used within supplied neighborhoods. General intersections receive a separate exhaustion and dimension-shift argument using the ordinary Euclidean cohomological-dimension bound.
The example uses the twisting-bundle definition, whose frame rule gives e₁=z⁻²e₀ for O(−2). It proves its cohomology calculation locally rather than importing a stronger scalar theorem.
Oka coherence is used to make the locally free rank-one twisting sheaf coherent; full AC is retained.

The projective-GAGA consumer's A4 preserves 0 ≤ r ≤ 3, all cohomological degrees, and the supplier's topology qualifications. Proof 5.2 uses finite dimensions to stabilize eventual surjections; full AC remains explicit.
